content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with cream sauce is a dish of cooked noodles tossed in a smooth sauce made from cream, butter, and often cheese. The creamy sauce gives the dish a velvety texture and rich flavor, while the variety of pasta shapes allows for many tasty combinations.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cream sauce originated in Italian cuisine in the 19th century as an alternative to tomato sauces.
Typical recipes use cream with a fat content of 20 %–35 % to achieve a thick consistency.
Any pasta shape can be used—spaghetti, fettuccine, penne—but broader noodles hold the sauce better.
The dish is traditionally finished with grated Parmesan or Pecorino, enhancing its aroma.
Variations may include mushrooms, spinach, salmon, or truffles in the sauce.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Pasta provides carbohydrates, a quick source of energy for the body.

items.title: Calcium from cream
items.content: Cream contains calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Durum wheat pasta supplies B1, B2, and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: When olive oil is added to the sauce, it contributes beneficial monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Both pasta and cheese provide plant‑based and dairy protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Cream sauces are rich in saturated fats, so the dish should be eaten in moderation, especially by those with cardiovascular concerns.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: Cream and cheese may cause discomfort for people with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional pasta contains gluten, making it unsuitable for individuals with celiac disease.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The meal is relatively calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Cream sauces often contain salt; those with hypertension should limit added salt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the pasta al dente, then toss it with hot cream sauce. Serve immediately, topped with grated cheese, freshly ground black pepper, and herbs. You can add sautéed vegetables, chicken, or seafood for extra variety.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry pasta in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Prepared sauce keeps in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Leftover pasta with sauce should be reheated gently on the stove, adding a splash of milk or cream to restore its creamy texture.
